Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Working diagnosis: Suspected transient ischemic attack (TIA) / ischemic cerebrovascular event; urgent evaluation planned
  - Conflict noted: Transcript supports urgent TIA referral; however the DDx notes TIAs are typically acute (minutes-hours) whereas the patient's episodes last days and resolve between events
- Other considerations from DDx aligned with transcript (listed for completeness but not confirmed):
  - Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) or other inflammatory demyelinating disease – moderate likelihood given episodic focal deficits in a young adult; no between-episode deficits described
  - Migraine with aura – possible if focal sensory symptoms occur with nausea; headaches not described
  - Brain tumor or other structural lesion – less likely given waxing/waning episodic pattern; not excluded
  - Vitamin B12 deficiency or other metabolic/vascular etiologies – not supported by available information
- Plan:
  - Refer to TIA clinic urgently for comprehensive evaluation
  - Investigations at TIA clinic likely to include carotid ultrasound and brain imaging (e.g., MRI/CT)
  - If symptoms recur or persist, seek emergency care (A&E)
  - Continue current aspirin 75 mg daily (dose/route/frequency documented; any changes not documented)
  - Provide patient with clinic contact numbers (PALS and TIA clinic) and instructions to contact if questions or recurrence
  - No other specific therapies initiated today pending specialist evaluation

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Transient ischemic attack / ischemic stroke (TIA/stroke)
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Episodic right-sided numbness/weakness with gait disturbance; increasing frequency of episodes; family history of stroke; clinician planned urgent TIA evaluation
  - Conflict noted: Patterns described (episodes lasting days with recovery between episodes) are atypical for classic TIAs
- Relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (MS) or other inflammatory demyelinating disease
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Young adult with focal neurological symptoms across episodes and fatigue
- Migraine with aura
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Paresthesias and transient focal deficits with nausea; absence of headache described
